dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: The dataset has been developed within the Arcadia Project. It concerns the processing of industrial tomatoes in reference to the report “Studio LCA della filiera dell’industria del pomodoro confezionato in Italia”.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: Italy. Primary data collected in the North. Representative dataset of North italian tomato chain production.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Early tomato varieties develop ripe fruit as early as three months after the first shoots appear, and there are also species that allow harvesting even earlier. Tomatoes are grown by farms located in the northern part of the peninsula. Farms are representative of the northern area of Italy. The main energy consumption is related to tillage and irrigation of the fields and phytosanitary treatment of tomato plants. Tomato harvesting can be done manually or using mechanized means, depending on the typology of packaging, of cultivation and the variety of tomato grown. Mechanized means specialize in selecting berries that conform to the required quality. Background data were modelled according to Ecoinvent v. 3.8
technology.technologicalApplicability: Tomato is an annual herbaceous plant. It is among the most widespread horticultural plants in the world. The fruits of this plant are used in the processing industry to produce concentrates, purees, peeled tomatoes, juices

review.common:reviewDetails:
The study is very representative from a geographical and technological point of view. From a temporal point of view, as the data refer to the two-year period 2020-2021, the representativeness is considered very good. For the North cultivation the completeness is considered very good.
The inventory data relating to the various processes within the system's boundaries are therefore to be considered reasonably representative of the supply chain under study, as they can to all intents and purposes be considered average data for the same. The quality of the data used in the study is considered to be good and the data were for the most part measured; where they were calculated or came from literature, they were all checked by experts. Allocation was avoided as far as possible by dividing the unitary process into two or more sub-processes and collecting environmental data on these sub-processes. When allocation could not be avoided, as in the case of products obtained during processing, the inputs and outputs of the system were divided between its different products and by-products. The allocation was generally based on mass (e.g. for waste treatment, waste water and energy used). The review was performed in compliance with Arcadia Metodology: “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA” and ISO 14040-44 norms. The dataset has been assessed limited to the foreground data collected during the supply chain studies. Each dataset has been evaluated based on the following 4 criteria: 1. Technological Representativeness; 2. Time Representativeness; 3. Geographical Representativeness; 4. Reliability (A) In this contest the Reliability is very good
